corpus.title: ‘We will not stop’: Students’ blunt message as school protests spread across France
corpus.signal_text:
‘We will not stop’: Students’ blunt message as school protests spread across France
More than 5,000 people have been arrested across the country this week as student demonstrations about overcrowded classrooms and school conditions turned violent. Jessie Williams reports

- CommentsGo to comments

This week France has been rocked by nationwide student protests that turned violent, with thousands arrested, more than 100 schools damaged and dozens of teachers injured.
By midday on Friday, the ministry of national education announced that 564 schools have been affected. Dramatic pictures show fires in the streets, barricaded entrance gates and youths clashing with riot police. At least four hundred high schools, roughly one in 10, were closed due to the unrest.
The protests began last week over frustrations about school conditions with peaceful blockades of secondary schools around Paris.
They soon morphed into wider discontent with the government and spread across the country, after France's main union for secondary school students called for a nationwide blockade. University students and other supporters also joined the demonstrations.
French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told TF1 TV on Friday that police had arrested a total of around 5,000 people, most of them teenagers, since Monday.
Justice Minister Darmanin had earlier told RTL radio that parents of those damaging property should pay reparations.
So far 65 school staff have been injured, including 40 headteachers, and there has been significant damage to facilities, with classes now taking place remotely, French education minister Édouard Geffray told French media on Friday. More than 300 police officers have also been injured in the chaos.
Students claim there has also been police violence against the protestors, with officers in riot gear using batons and tear gas.
In Tours, a city in central France, a 16-year-old student was injured on Wednesday outside his secondary school after being hit in the eye with an LBD-40 – Lanceur de Balles de Défense or Defence Ball Launcher. The controversial riot gun used by French police has caused severe injuries at previous protests.
